purpose: Evidence-first registry of AI backends that Brain may evaluate and use as replaceable adapters.

recommended.why_add: Open-source, provider-agnostic, supports local models and multiple interfaces.
Strong general software-development agent with Docker/runtime execution and local-model support.
Useful MCP-oriented alternative for tool orchestration and replaceable model backends.
Adds a Qwen-oriented coding-agent path and complements the Brain's Asia/global model strategy.
Provides a simple local inference path so Brain can operate without mandatory paid model APIs.
OpenAI-compatible serving path for higher-throughput self-hosted models.
Candidate security boundary for autonomous agents; must be evaluated before production adoption.
Open-source MIT model checkpoints for translation across 22 scheduled Indian languages; strong multilingual adapter for Brain.
Open-source MIT ASR suite covering 22 official Indian languages; useful for multilingual voice input.
Open-source MIT transliteration models for 21 Indic languages; useful for mixed Latin/Indic input normalization.
Open-source MIT language-identification component for Indian languages; useful before routing translation and speech pipelines.
Current Sarvam documentation exposes an open-source model pool; Brain should benchmark individual models and verify their exact licenses before production use.

Open-source AI4Bharat project for Indic video transcription, translation and voice-over; useful for Brain's cinematic localization pipeline. License and model-level terms must be verified before production.

Japan-based open research project focused on LLM-driven evolutionary improvement of algorithms; useful as a research candidate for Brain's bounded self-improvement layer, not an autonomous production dependency.
Japan-based orchestration approach that dynamically coordinates multiple models and agents; evaluate as an optional architecture reference/adapter.
Taiwanese MediaTek Research Breeze ASR work provides an open model path for Taigi/Hokkien speech recognition, expanding Brain's Asian-language voice coverage.
Taiwan-LLM provides open models tuned for Traditional Mandarin and English, including Llama-3-Taiwan variants; useful for Traditional Chinese localization and regional evaluation.
recommended.license: Llama-3 license for listed Llama-3-Taiwan models

recommended.why_add: Upstage's open-weight 250B/15B-active MoE is explicitly designed for agentic work, tool calling and coding, with Korean, English and Japanese support; suitable as a benchmark/cloud adapter rather than a phone-local dependency.
Open-source PaddleOCR provides a practical Chinese-origin OCR path for documents, screenshots and multilingual text extraction in Brain pipelines.

DeepSeek and Huawei are open-sourcing tooling around Ascend AI chips; this is worth tracking as an alternative compute stack, but it should remain an experimental adapter until Brain validates hardware availability and reproducibility.
Mistral's public Vibe project adds a European coding-agent option that can be benchmarked alongside Brain's existing coding-agent backends.
OpenEuroLLM is building transparent multilingual foundation models with openly documented data, training and evaluation components; useful for Brain's European-language sovereign-model adapter.
OpenLLM France provides open French-focused models and datasets, including edge-oriented and larger model sizes; useful for French and European-language routing.

not_auto_selected: Models or services that require payment are adapters only and never core dependencies.
Experimental agents are benchmark candidates until Brain records independent evidence.
No backend is trusted merely because its process exits successfully.
